What is it like to be a poor student at a very rich university or high school?

Depends on the culture of the school/program and how poor you want to talk about (not that I was poor in absolute terms but we weren't as well off as most of my classmates in both high school and college). High school is easier in some ways and tougher in others. In high school you care more about the relative differences between yourself and others but the reality of those differences is not as large. In college you care less because it's easier to find a selective peer group but the differences are much more real. In high school what might amount to having a car, fancier clothes, and cooler stories about summer vacations becomes living off campus, not having to work through school, and having more employment opportunities or any for that matter lined up after graduation. In high school by and large (so long as absolute poverty doesn't become a concern e.g. you have to work to feed your family) you have many of the same opportunities up to a point. My high school would go out of its way to ensure no one was excluded for financial reasons (we had a big disparity in wealth for a public school). In college for the most part people don't give a shit about you. If you can't afford to do that activity you just won't get to do it but it's easier to find other students to hang out with who have similar economic backgrounds. That being said to reiterate in absolute terms I did not grow up poor we were just less well off than most of my friends by a good bit.
